articles.title: For two years of my teenage life I did not look in a mirror
articles.deck: She wanted to be a doctor, followed her friends into a diploma she did not understand, and then heard a voice tell her to resign a job she had held for thirteen months. She ended up running a theological college.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the March-April 2014 issue, pages 4 and 5, where it ran unsigned as the cover story and is almost entirely in her own voice. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected. One claim has been recast as her own recollection rather than as established fact: that she was the only woman then principal of an Asia Theological Association college in India. It is not verifiable now and was self-reported then. Readers should also know that Trinity Christian College, which she led, took a full-page advertisement in this same issue.

body.v: Stella Bogi of Hyderabad graduated with an M.Th in Pastoral Theology in 2000 and was Principal of Trinity Christian College, Hyderabad, when this was published. She studied at SAIACS in Bangalore, and taught at Trinity first as a part-time lecturer, then full-time, then as Vice-Principal, then as Principal.

One afternoon I saw Jesus, just like we see him in the movies, with white clothes, long hair, beard, signalling me with his hand to follow him. I followed him without any fear or hesitation, a few steps, and then he disappeared. I ran and told this to my mother and my mom said, next time He calls you, say "here am I".
So far I have not seen Him.
The girl in the kitchen

I grew up with five other siblings: two older brothers, two younger brothers and one younger sister. At an early age, since my mother was a working woman, I had the responsibility of taking care of my younger siblings.
I could not bear when difference was shown between the boys and girls at home. I wanted justice. I would speak out and say, if girls can do washing then boys can do too.

Though I spoke up boldly, which was my defence mechanism, I was actually very timid and shy, with very low self-esteem. I hated the way I looked and thought there was no good in me, and therefore was always found in the kitchen. I hated myself so much that for two years of my teenage life I did not look in the mirror.
I hated myself so much that for two years of my teenage life I did not look in the mirror.
body.highlight: I did not look in the mirror

body.v: My parents gave us a very good, God-fearing atmosphere at home. The bedtime stories my mom told us were from the Bible. The first Bible study I remember was from the book of Nehemiah, taught by my dad.

While studying in 10th class I had a great desire to be a Sunday School teacher. While I was preparing my first Sunday school lesson I was born again, when I came to the portion of "How to lead a child to Christ" from one of the CEF story books.
Since I grew up with very low self esteem, I needed to be appreciated. So I put all my energies into developing my cooking skills and into studies.
The wrong diploma, and then a voice

I was a very bright student and wanted to become a doctor. But God had a different path carved out for me. Since my friends from my 12th class went to do a Diploma in Commercial Practice, I also joined the crowd without knowing what it was. Even before I could get my results I got a job in a Christian printing press.
I was actively involved in preaching in the church my father had started, and in other churches, in Vacation Bible School, youth meetings, Sunday Schools and Good News clubs.

I had completed working for one year and one month. It was 23rd September 1984. I heard an audible voice: "Resign." I knew it was for me. So I told my Managing Director I was resigning since the Lord had asked me to. He tried to increase my salary, but in vain.

I shared this news with my pastor, Amos Jayarathnam, who asked me to confirm this word from the Lord. On 24th September 1984, at my first fasting prayer, I began to seek the Lord. After some time I heard an audible voice: "Read Isaiah 61:6."

I opened my eyes, looked at the closed Bible beside me and thought, how can there be 66 chapters? I had no idea then about the chapters. I heard the voice a second time. I opened my eyes and thought, what if I open the Bible and there are no 66 chapters? And I began to cry and pray more. I could not resist the voice the third time, as it was very powerful and loud, and I turned to it.
And you will be called priests of the Lord, you will be named ministers of our God. You will feed on the wealth of the nations and in their riches you will boast.
I knew this was a direct call from the Lord.
Nobody had told her women could go

For a year I accompanied my pastor to village ministries and other places. Then in July 1985, one of our church youth boys had returned from his studies in Bible college. He suggested that I join the Bible college.
Until then I had no idea that women too could go to Bible college.
Until then I had no idea that women too could go to Bible college.

I prayed and asked the Lord that if it was His will, He would open the door for me, as the admissions had closed one month back. On 14th July 1985 I joined Bharat Bible College, and by 1990 had completed a Bachelor of Theology and a Bachelor of Divinity. I knew I was called to be a teacher. Teaching is my passion.

I was involved in pioneering a Bible college in Bangalore and then in teaching there for two years, from 1994 to 1996. Then I came to Hyderabad, and since then have been involved in teaching and administration at Trinity Christian College.
The only one

It was a shock to me to learn that, as far as I knew, I was the only woman principal in India among the Asia Theological Association colleges. My prayer is that there will be many women in leadership positions in theological institutions in India.

Any society is recognised by the values it has. I strongly believe that if a society has to be developed, then the women have to be developed. Women influence their families, and the families in turn influence the society. Thus a society with good standing is formed.
The standard of a society is directly proportional to the value of a woman at home.
body.highlight: directly proportional to the value of a woman

articles.title: Every giant introduces a man to himself, and mine was a small, polite church secretary
articles.deck: He was twenty-one and running the youth programme. She did not like how he was doing it and told everyone except him. Three things a pastor of thirty-nine years has learned about the things that tower over us.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the March-April 2014 issue, pages 8 and 9. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is the author's throughout. Three things in it are wrong or uncredited, and rather than alter his text they are set right in a note at the foot: the book he cites is misnamed, the statistics attached to it do not come from that book, and the sentence he attributes to Booker T. Washington is not what Washington wrote.

body.v: All of us face them: those situations or people that seem to tower over us, sometimes leaving us paralyzed in our tracks and sometimes running for our lives.

Whenever I think of giants I think of one of the greatest stories in the Bible, the story of young David facing big Goliath, the champion of the Philistines, who stood over 9 feet tall and daily threatened the army of God. You can find his story in the Old Testament book of 1 Samuel 17.

It truly is an amazing story that took place in the Valley of Elah many, many years ago, yet contains timely life and leadership lessons for us today, regardless of the culture in which we live. Here are three giant statements about giants.
1. Every giant introduces a person to himself
Every time you or I face a giant it reveals a lot about who we are. Whether a personal crisis, a person, or an overwhelming problem, that giant serves as a mirror to help me see myself.

I remember one of the first ministry giants I faced was in the form of a tiny, petite lady in our church who happened to be the wife of one of the leaders in the church and the church secretary. To get to the point, she didn't like the way I was running the youth program and proceeded to discuss it with everyone else but me. Essentially she was undermining everything I did.

Realizing this just couldn't continue, I mustered up all the courage I could as a young kid of 21 years of age, and confronted her on the issue. I shared with her how what she was doing was hurting my ministry and how I needed her support as a person of influence in the church.
I'm happy to say that she responded favorably and as a result I not only gained her support but also her respect.

Someone has said, "The size of a person is measured by the size of the challenges he or she is willing to face." You see, a lot of times, rather than face the giant we choose to run from it, ignore it, or just pretend it doesn't exist.

That giant encounter helped me learn that every giant I was ever going to face in life was going to reintroduce me to myself. And when I faced them and dealt with them appropriately, though not always successfully, I could walk away with a certain amount of self-respect. I could say to myself, "George, that took courage. Way to go! You were not sure how that was going to turn out but you faced it! Good job."
A challenge doesn't make us. It only reveals the stuff of which we are made.
body.highlight: reveals the stuff of which we are made

body.v: 2. People growing to their highest potential have defeated giants
It is true about sports teams, business teams, church leadership teams, marriages, families. No one will ever be all they can be without somewhere, sometime facing and overcoming great obstacles.

In 1962 a book was published that is now out of print called Cradles of Imminence. It was a book that studied the lives of 413 famous and successful people for five years, attempting to discover a common thread in their life that would show why they were so successful.

After five years of close examination, it was noted that of the 413 people, 392 of them had faced unbelievable problems in their life. And they began to realize that the people who were coming out on top were the people who had been under overwhelming odds.
Booker T. Washington, the great African-American educator, once said: "You cannot ever judge success by what position you have, you can only judge success by what you had to overcome to get there."
3. Giants are often tools God uses to shape us for bigger things
Giants are tools God uses to make us better people, stronger people, and more mature people.

In the story of David and Goliath, it was not uncommon for one man to represent an army. They did that so there would not be a major loss of life. Each army would send forth their champion and put him up against the opposing army's warrior. And whichever army won, the other would submit to a certain period of slavery.
In other words, the giant represented something much bigger than just himself. He represented the whole army.
Likewise, the giants you and I face seldom stand alone. Most problems you and I face represent a lot more than just what we are encountering or what we are seeing at the moment.
An important lesson for you and me is simply this: when a giant defeats us, others close to us suffer too. However, when we overcome the giants in our life, others enjoy the victory and are blessed.
So ask yourself, what giant am I facing today? What are you discovering about yourself? How are you growing through this challenge? What is God building in your life in the process?

Three corrections, printed here rather than made silently in the author's text. The 1962 book is Cradles of Eminence, not Imminence, by Victor and Mildred Goertzel; its own subtitle describes a study of over four hundred famous twentieth-century men and women. The 413 and 392 figures, and the five years of study, are a sermon-illustration commonplace that circulates widely and cannot be traced to the Goertzels' book. And Booker T. Washington's actual sentence, from Up from Slavery in 1901, is: "I have learned that success is to be measured not so much by the position that one has reached in life as by the obstacles which he has overcome while trying to succeed." The version quoted here is a modern rewording in circulation, not his words. The heading of the first point also appears word for word in a published sermon on 1 Samuel 17 that predates this article.

articles.title: An empty lampstand looks exactly like a full one until the room goes dark
articles.deck: God gave Moses the dimensions of a tent and specified the oil for its lamps. Three thousand years later the question the tent was asking is still the only one that matters: where does your light come from?

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the March-April 2014 issue, pages 17 to 20, under the heading "Convergence". Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is the author's throughout. One correction: the 2014 page spelled her name Stevec. It is Svetec, as it appeared correctly on her two earlier pieces in this magazine.

body.v: From the moment God made our world with those marvellous words, "Let there be light", God has been invading our darkness with His Light, and He has never stopped.

Years after Adam and Noah, centuries later, God chose a people to carry His light. One day He grabbed Abraham and pulled him into relationship, saying, "Go to the land I will show you." In Canaan, on three different occasions, the Lord urges Abraham:
Look up at the heavens and count the stars, if indeed you can count them. So shall your offspring be.
God plans to use His kids as His spectacular stars that shine and illuminate the darkness. A sign and a wonder as lights in darkness, started back then and continuing today.
Daniel, in an occult kingdom
In ancient days, Daniel, standing tall as one of a few believers in a dark occult-controlled kingdom, understood his destiny to shine.
Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars for ever and ever.

Daniel declared God as worthy of worship in every situation and would not relent in his prayers despite deadly persecution. In turn, God shifted kingdoms, established the captives' return, and revealed end-time visions to His beloved servant.
The worship manifesto
When Moses ushered the million Jews out of Egypt, God then established worship as a daily morning and evening practice. Painstakingly God outlined the blueprints for the tabernacle.
Make this tabernacle and all its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.
Central to the camp, the twelve tribes camped around its hub, as life flowed from the tabernacle of God where the priests of God daily worshipped Him.
Out in the outer court there were two objects: the burnt offering altar for the sacrifices, and the brass basin for washing.

Inside the tabernacle, in the Holy Place, there were three key items: the table of the showbread, with twelve loaves for the twelve tribes of Israel, replaced daily; the table with incense, trimmed and lit morning and evening; and the lampstand with pressed holy olive oil for fuel, lit morning and evening.

Inside the inner sanctum, the Holy of Holies, there was the ark of the covenant with the two cherubim, of which God said that there, above the cover between the two cherubim, He would meet with them and give all His commands for the Israelites. Inside that area was a jar of manna, kept for the generations to come so they could see the bread He gave them in the desert. Aaron's perpetually budding almond stick was placed before the Testimony. And the Ten Commandments, two stone tablets scribed by God's hand, were placed inside the ark.
So why care about a tent in a desert
Why care about something established in the desert over three thousand years ago? The writer of Hebrews explains.

We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, and who serves in the sanctuary, the true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man... They serve at a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: "See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."
The tabernacle God set up with Moses was a copy or a shadow of what is in heaven. So in this tent of meeting there is revelation of heaven's own tent of meeting.
The city on a hill

Now when Jesus walked the earth, He taught His friends that He was the Light of the World. All our light comes from Him. And He taught us to pray: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden. Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand and it gives light to everyone in the house. In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and praise your Father in heaven.
Jesus was speaking to his nation, the Jewish nation. For every child of Israel standing there, the only city that mattered was Jerusalem, Israel's crown jewel.

King David, with the Lord of hosts, and Joab and the army, wrestled Zion from the Jebusites. God gloriously established the city of David and his lineage to rule and reign perpetually. Centuries later Jerusalem fell to the Babylonians and was restored by Ezra, Nehemiah and Zerubbabel. History records it fell again to Greece and then to Rome. Sixteen times Jerusalem has been fought for.
It still stands as Israel's sign and wonder, and for thousands of years has stood as a testimony of God's provision and protection.

When Jesus used Jerusalem as his example, it was like Jesus was waving Israel's flag, asking: do you remember whose you are? Do you remember your testimony as a nation chosen by God? Do you remember your purpose? Be light. Be light in the darkness.
A lamp is a practical object

Remember the tent of meeting that Moses so carefully established at God's command? Inside the temple, the permanent tent established by David, then Solomon, and then erected as a monument by Herod, in Jesus' day there still stood the lampstand, the incense, the showbread of heaven's decree.

Both the holy menorah and the lampstand were practical items, like a flashlight is today, bringing illumination and sight to darkened places. In Jesus' day electricity had not yet been invented, so the household oil lamp lit the whole house. The lamp had practical purpose: to bring light to dispel the darkness, to cook, to visit, to study, to celebrate, to live.

The menorah stood as a reminder of our darkness without God who is Light. It was tended daily, replenished with fuel as often as needed, a perpetual testimony of God with us, and us in God. Life flowed, despite darkness, when the lampstand was lit.

Through these two pictures, Jesus was asking: do you remember your holy purpose to shine? Do men see your holy walk of love and then praise the God who has empowered you to love? Are you light in the darkness? Are you light in your home? Are you light in your workplace, in your business, in your nation? Do you understand you are a lampstand? Do you know where your Light comes from?
The oil is the point

In that tent of meeting, the holy lampstand bore seven branches, representing the Holy Spirit. The lamp bore seven wicks which shone day and night. These wicks only shone if they had the fuel required: the holy oil, pressed olive oil, the symbol of Israel all through the scriptures.

God our Father dreams about us, a breed redeemed and full of Christ Jesus, fuelled by His Spirit, burning with wisdom, counsel, knowledge, fear of God, might and understanding, burning through Him, with Him and in Him, in the unity of the Holy Spirit for God's glory.

Do everything without complaining or arguing, so that you may become blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and depraved generation, in which you shine like stars in the universe as you hold out the word of life.
Or are you an empty lampstand, looking good but running on empty? Have you stayed there in the well-lit church, an ancient lamp without oil?
body.highlight: looking good but running on empty

body.v: Do you have the oil of God, the Holy Spirit, to burn bright in the darkness? It's time to be filled with the oil of God once more.
To be light in the darkness and shine bright with love, to be of practical help and holy love for those in darkness, much oil is required.

Thank God for the patterns He reveals in Scripture. The Holy Spirit is the oil of God. We are designed to shine with the fuel of God. He made us this way. To love is to be light. John the beloved stated this emphatically.

No one has seen God, ever. But if we love one another, God dwells deeply within us, and his love becomes complete in us, perfect love! This is how we know we're living steadily and deeply in him, and he in us: He's given us life from his life, from his very own Spirit.

Holy Spirit of God, would you fill us that we may shine with the love of God and be a practical solution in the dark around us? Lord Jesus, as we love you, as You have loved us, would your light, O Light of the World, burn through us? O Father God, abide in us as we abide in Christ. By your grace, make us burn bright in the darkness.
May the convergence of the Holy Spirit spark the flame, that we may shine bright with Jesus, Light of the World, for those in darkness.
Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own.
How bright are you shining?
